title: Merge PDF
dek: Combine several PDFs into one document. Drag them into the order you want, or let the file list decide.
meta: Merge multiple PDF files into one document, free and offline. Files are combined in your browser — nothing is uploaded, no sign-up needed.

steps.p: Drop two or more PDF files onto the cutting board. They stay in your browser the whole time.
New files land at the bottom. Use the arrows on each file to move it up or down.
Press Merge. The combined file downloads straight away.

faq.q: Is there a file size limit?
faq.a: No hard limit from us. The practical ceiling is your computer's memory — a merge of a few 100 MB files is usually fine on a modern laptop.

faq.q: What about password-protected PDFs?
faq.a: Those can't be opened without the password, so they can't be merged. Unlock them first, then merge.

title: Split PDF
h1: Split a PDF into separate files
dek: Cut one PDF into several. Split at every page, or pull out just the ranges you name.
meta: Split a PDF into multiple files by page ranges, offline in your browser. No uploads, no email wall. Free and private.

steps.p: One file at a time. The page count is shown as soon as it loads.
Every page becomes its own file, or type ranges like 1-3, 4, 7-9 to choose exactly what gets cut out.
You'll get each piece as its own PDF, plus a ZIP button if you'd rather take them all at once.

faq.q: How do I split at a certain page?
faq.a: Use ranges: '1-5, 6-10' gives you two files, one for each range. '1,2,3' gives you three single-page files.

faq.q: Does splitting change the pages?
faq.a: No. Pages are copied exactly as they are — text stays text, images stay sharp.

title: Extract PDF Pages
dek: Pull selected pages out of a PDF into a new document, without touching the original file.
meta: Extract specific pages from a PDF into a new file, right in your browser. Free, offline, no uploads or accounts.

steps.p: The tool reads the page count so you know what you're working with.
Type a selection like 2,5,6-9. That order is kept in the new file.
You get a fresh PDF with only those pages. The original on disk is never modified.

faq.q: Can I extract pages in reverse order?
faq.a: Yes — '9-6' works and writes the pages back to front. Type it exactly as 9-6.

faq.q: How is this different from splitting?
faq.a: Splitting cuts one PDF into many. Extracting pulls a selection into one new file and leaves it at that.

title: Delete PDF Pages
dek: Drop the pages you don't want — blank scans, cover sheets, that one page with the wrong total.
meta: Remove unwanted pages from a PDF and save the cleaned file, all offline in your browser. Free, private, no uploads.

steps.p: The total page count appears so you can double-check against the document.
Type numbers or ranges, like 1,4,7-9. Everything else stays untouched.
You get a new PDF; the original on your disk stays as it was.

faq.q: Can I delete the first page only?
faq.a: Type 1 and press the button. That's it.

faq.q: What if I remove every page?
faq.a: The tool refuses — a PDF needs at least one page — and tells you so instead of producing a broken file.

title: Rotate PDF
dek: Scanned a batch sideways again? Turn every page or just the odd ones, then save.
meta: Rotate PDF pages 90, 180 or 270 degrees and save — entirely in your browser, no uploads. Fix sideways scans in seconds.

steps.p: Load the sideways document.
90° clockwise or anticlockwise, or 180° to flip it right over. Optionally limit this to certain pages.
The rotation is written into the file, so it shows the same everywhere.

faq.q: Can I rotate only page 3?
faq.a: Yes. Leave the rotation set, type 3 in the pages box, and only that page turns.

faq.q: Does rotating hurt quality?
faq.a: No. Rotation is a note written into the page — no re-rendering, no pixel damage.

title: Reorder PDF Pages
dek: The page order the scanner chose, or the one you actually want. Rearrange and save.
meta: Rearrange PDF pages into any order — type the new sequence, get the file back in seconds. Offline, free, no uploads.

steps.p: Check the page count that appears.
For a 5-page file, '5,4,3,2,1' reverses it. '2,1,3,4,5' swaps the first two. Every page must appear exactly once.
The rearranged file downloads with nothing else changed.

faq.q: What if I get the sequence wrong?
faq.a: The tool checks it against the page count and refuses with a plain-English message rather than silently skipping pages.

faq.q: Can I duplicate a page this way?
faq.a: No — reordering only moves pages. Use Extract Pages twice if you need a duplicate.

title: Compress PDF
dek: Shrink oversized PDFs for email and upload limits. Choose how hard to squeeze and watch the size drop.
meta: Compress PDF files in your browser — pick a quality level, see before/after sizes, download instantly. No uploads, free.

steps.p: The current file size is shown so you can compare after.
Light keeps near-original quality. Balanced is the sensible default. Strong squeezes hardest for the smallest file.
You'll see exactly how many MB disappeared before you save.

faq.q: How does it work?
faq.a: Light mode optimises the file's structure and keeps text as text. Balanced and Strong re-render pages as high-quality images at a lower resolution — like re-photographing the pages at a sensible size. Strong on a photo-heavy scan can cut 90% or more.

faq.q: Will text stay selectable?
faq.a: In Light mode, yes. In Balanced and Strong the pages become images, so text is no longer selectable — that's the trade for the smaller size.

faq.q: My file barely shrank. Why?
faq.a: PDFs that are already optimised (mostly plain text) have almost nothing to give. Try Strong, or accept that some files are simply already small.

title: PDF to JPG
dek: Turn each page into a JPG image. Pick the resolution — 150 DPI for screens, 300 DPI for print.
meta: Convert PDF pages to JPG images at up to 300 DPI, right in your browser. Private, offline, no uploads or sign-up.

steps.p: Works best on documents up to a few hundred pages.
DPI sets the sharpness; the pages field lets you convert only a selection.
Single page converts download directly; more than one arrives as a ZIP.

faq.q: What DPI should I use?
faq.a: 150 DPI is fine for viewing and email. 300 DPI is the print standard. 72 DPI only if you truly need thumbnails.

faq.q: Why is my output blurry?
faq.a: It isn't — check your DPI setting. At 72 DPI a full A4 page is only 595 pixels wide; that's the setting, not the conversion.

title: PDF to PNG
dek: Sharp, lossless page images — good for screenshots, slides and anything you'll edit afterwards.
meta: Convert PDF pages to PNG images at custom DPI in your browser. Lossless quality, zero uploads, completely free.

steps.p: Every page is rendered on your machine.
300 DPI for print-sharp, 150 for everyday use. Restrict to specific pages if you like.
A single page downloads as one PNG; several pages come zipped.

faq.q: PNG or JPG — which should I pick?
faq.a: PNG for crisp text and line art, JPG for photo-heavy pages where file size matters more than perfection.

faq.q: Transparent background?
faq.a: Most PDFs paint a white page, and the converter honours that. Pages with no background come out transparent.

title: PDF to Text
dek: Get the words out — editable, selectable, copyable — with page markers so nothing gets lost in the shuffle.
meta: Extract selectable text from PDF files in your browser. Copy it or download as .txt. No uploads, free, works offline.

steps.p: The tool reads the text layer, page by page.
Text appears in the box below with --- page --- markers. Copy what you need, or take the whole thing as .txt.
One click for the whole document; the copy button is there for a single paragraph.

faq.q: The text came out empty. Why?
faq.a: That PDF is a scan — it's a picture of text, not text itself. Use the OCR tool to read scans.

faq.q: Are tables and columns preserved?
faq.a: Roughly. Text comes out in reading order, so simple tables survive and complex multi-column layouts may need tidying.

title: Images to PDF
dek: JPG, PNG or WebP in — one tidy PDF out. Set the page size, margins, and whether each image fills its page.
meta: Combine JPG, PNG and WebP images into a single PDF with custom page size and margins. Offline in your browser, no uploads.

steps.p: Most formats work: JPG, PNG, WebP, GIF (first frame), BMP. They're ordered as listed.
A4 or Letter, portrait or landscape, and whether images fit inside the margin or fill the whole page.
One PDF with your images, in order.

faq.q: Will my images be re-compressed?
faq.a: No. They're embedded as-is, so quality is exactly what you dropped in — the PDF is simply a tidy container.

faq.q: Can I reorder the images?
faq.a: Yes — remove and re-add, or drop them in the order you want. The list order is the page order.

title: Watermark PDF
h1: Add a watermark to a PDF
dek: Stamp text across the pages — DRAFT, CONFIDENTIAL, your company name — at the angle and opacity you set.
meta: Add text watermarks to PDF pages with custom size, angle and opacity. Runs in your browser — no uploads, free, private.

steps.p: The page count and size are read automatically.
Type your text, then set size, colour, opacity and angle. Diagonal and faint is the classic look; your call.
The watermark is drawn on every page you choose.

faq.q: Can I watermark only some pages?
faq.a: Yes — type the pages to cover, like 1-3,7. Leave it blank for every page.

faq.q: Can I use a logo image as a watermark?
faq.a: Text only for now. Image watermarks need alpha handling that would bloat this page without adding much.

title: Page Numbers PDF
h1: Add page numbers to a PDF
dek: Number your pages properly — position, start number and format like 1 or Page 1 of 12.
meta: Add page numbers to any PDF with custom position, start number and format like 'Page 3 of 20'. In-browser, free, no uploads.

steps.p: Page count is read so the 'of N' style can be accurate.
Pick the corner, the first number, font size, and whether to include 'of N'.
Numbers appear exactly where you placed them, on every chosen page.

faq.q: Can I skip the cover page?
faq.a: Yes. Set the start number and choose which pages receive numbers — leave page 1 out and start counting at 1 on page 2.

faq.q: Which corners can I use?
faq.a: Six positions: three along the bottom, three along the top.

title: PDF Metadata Editor
dek: Fix the title, author and keywords that applications show for a PDF — or clear leftovers before sharing the file.
meta: View and edit PDF title, author, subject and keywords — or wipe the metadata clean before sharing. Free, offline, private.

steps.p: The current title, author, subject and keywords are read out and shown in the fields.
Change anything you like. Empty fields are removed from the file, not written as blanks.
Only metadata changes; the pages are untouched.

faq.q: What gets shown to readers?
faq.a: The title appears in the browser tab and some readers; the author and keywords show up in file properties and search indexes.

faq.q: Can this hide that a PDF was edited?
faq.a: No, and it isn't meant to. It fixes metadata — dates and producer records are left alone.

title: PDF to Word
dek: Get the text into a .docx you can edit. No layout magic promised — words come out clean and ready to reformat.
meta: Convert a PDF to an editable Word .docx with text pulled page by page. Honest, browser-based, no sign-up, no uploads.

steps.p: Text is pulled page by page, keeping paragraph breaks where the PDF has them.
Optionally keep page markers so you can find your place while editing.
Open it in Word, Google Docs, LibreOffice — whatever you have.

faq.q: Will it look exactly like the PDF?
faq.a: No, and no honest browser tool can promise that. Layout, columns and images aren't reproduced — the text and paragraphs are. You'll reformat in seconds; you won't retype in hours.

faq.q: My scan produced an empty document.
faq.a: Scanned PDFs have no text layer. Run the OCR tool first, then paste the result — or rebuild the document in Word directly.
